name: MonarchLogViewer
title: LogViewer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of monospaced lines with androidx.compose.ui.input.nestedscroll.NestedScrollConnection for pausing; MonarchSearchBar, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip for the levels, Follow and Wrap lines, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchLoadingState
summary: A streaming log with level filters and counts, search that filters or highlights, follow mode that keeps the newest line in view, and a wrap toggle.
whenToUse: To watch the output of a deployment, a job run or a service as it streams, or to read back a finished run's log.
whenNotToUse: For one log entry's full record use the LogDrawer recipe (a sheet with a description list and code block). For static code use MonarchCodeBlock.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchLogViewer(lines: List<MonarchLogLine>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, levels: Set<MonarchLogLevel>? = null, onLevelsChange: ((Set<MonarchLogLevel>) -> Unit)? = null, query: String? = null, onQueryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, following: Boolean? = null, onFollowingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, wrapped: Boolean? = null, onWrappedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, searchMode: MonarchLogViewerSearchMode = MonarchLogViewerSearchMode.Filter, showTimestamps: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), clearSearchIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchLogViewerLabels = MonarchLogViewerLabels(), actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
public data class MonarchLogLine(id: String, message: String, level: MonarchLogLevel = MonarchLogLevel.Info, time: Long? = null, source: String? = null)
public enum class MonarchLogLevel { Debug, Info, Warn, Error }
public enum class MonarchLogViewerSearchMode { Filter, Highlight }

public class MonarchLogViewerLabels(log: String? = null, levels: String? = null, levelName: ((level: MonarchLogLevel) -> String)? = null, search: String? = null, clearSearch: String? = null, follow: String? = null, wrap: String? = null, count: ((shown: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, jumpToLatest: String? = null, newLines: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, followPaused: String? = null, followResumed: String? = null, empty: String? = null, noMatches: String? = null, clearFilters: String? = null, loading: String? = null)

options.name: lines
options.description: The lines, oldest first. Append to the list to stream.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the viewer. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: levels
options.description: The levels shown. Kept inside, with all four on at first, when null.

options.name: onLevelsChange
options.description: Called when a level filter is toggled or the filters are cleared.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text. Kept inside when null. Trimmed and matched against the message and the source, ignoring case.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Called on every edit and when the filters are cleared.

options.name: following
options.description: Whether the newest line is kept in view. Kept inside, on at first, when null.

options.name: onFollowingChange
options.description: Called with false when the reader drags toward older lines or turns Follow off, and with true when they return to the end, tap the jump button or turn Follow on.

options.name: wrapped
options.description: Whether long lines wrap. Kept inside, off at first, when null. Unwrapped lines scroll sideways.

options.name: onWrappedChange
options.description: Called when Wrap lines is toggled.

options.name: searchMode
options.description: Filter hides lines without a match; Highlight keeps every line. Both mark the matches.

options.name: showTimestamps
options.description: Shows each line's time as 24-hour HH:mm:ss.SSS in the device's time zone.

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Shows each line's 1-based position in lines, which stays the same when filters hide lines.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows Loading log while lines is empty.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the log.

options.name: clearSearchIcon
options.description: An icon for the search field's clear button, named Clear search; without it the field has no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the level names, the count and the jump button.

options.name: actions
options.description: Extra controls after Follow and Wrap lines, such as Share or Clear.

states.name: following
states.description: Every change of the lines scrolls the log to the newest one. Follow is selected.

states.name: paused
states.description: The log stays where the reader is. A Jump to latest button floats over the bottom of the log and reads "3 new lines" when lines arrive.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Long lines wrap inside the width; otherwise each line is one row and the log scrolls sideways.

states.name: filtered
states.description: The footer reads "2 of 5 lines". When nothing is left, a filtered MonarchEmptyState offers Clear filters, which empties the search and turns every level back on.

states.name: loading
states.description: MonarchLoadingState's spinner with Loading log while there are no lines yet.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState, No log lines yet.

appearance: The log sits on the subtle background in the code type, one row per line. The level is a word in semibold, coloured by level (muted for debug, the strong info, warning and danger roles); warning and error rows have the subtle warning or danger fill. Times, line numbers and sources are muted. Matches are underlined on the subtle accent fill. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web LogViewer measures and virtualises rows itself; on Android a LazyColumn composes only the rows in view. The web pauses following from the scroll position; here a drag toward older lines (a nested scroll from user input) pauses it and coming to rest at the end of the log resumes it, as on iOS. Home and End keys are not offered; Follow and the jump button do the same. The time is fixed to HH:mm:ss.SSS in the device's time zone and cannot be replaced (the web's formatTime). The web's estimatedRowHeight, overscan and atBottomThreshold have no meaning with a LazyColumn. The level filters, Follow and Wrap lines are Material 3 FilterChips rather than a segmented toggle group, so they wrap onto new rows on a narrow phone and at large text sizes. Monarch bundles no icons, so the search field's clear button appears only with clearSearchIcon. Android uses the same name and API shape as iOS, with a value and an on…Change callback for each binding.
accessibility: Each line is one element read as its level, time, source and message.
The level filters are a group named "Levels"; each filter is a FilterChip with the selected state, read with its count.
Follow and Wrap lines are FilterChips with the selected state.
Pausing and resuming following are announced through a polite live region: "Following paused" and "Following new lines".
Search matches are underlined as well as tinted, and the level is written as a word, so neither relies on color.
The chips and the jump button have 48dp touch targets; the toolbar mirrors in right-to-left layouts while the lines read left to right.
edgeCases: Lines without a time leave out the time column; lines without a source leave out the source.
Long lines without wrap make the whole log scroll sideways.
Ids must be unique and stable: they are the keys of the rows.
The viewer takes the height it is given and scrolls inside it: do not put it in another vertical scroll.
Line numbers keep their positions in the full list, so a filtered log shows gaps.
TalkBack scrolling is not a drag: it does not pause following; turn Follow off to read back.

examples.title: Search that highlights, with filters the app keeps
examples.setup:
var levels by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf(MonarchLogLevel.Warn, MonarchLogLevel.Error)) }
var query by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("timeout") }
examples.code:
MonarchLogViewer(
    lines = listOf(MonarchLogLine("1", "Upstream timeout after 30 s", MonarchLogLevel.Error)),
    modifier = Modifier.height(MonarchTheme.spacing.space24 * 4),
    levels = levels,
    onLevelsChange = { levels = it },
    query = query,
    onQueryChange = { query = it },
    searchMode = MonarchLogViewerSearchMode.Highlight,
)

parityExceptions.reason: The log is a lazy list that composes only the lines in view and follows the newest line, as the web viewer does; the older lines are scrolled out of view, not removed.
parityExceptions.convention: virtualised list: only visible rows exist
